answer: Treat each agent reputation as a vertex in a trust graph, not an island: a vertex gains weight only through bidirectional, costly attestations from established peers, so a Sybil cluster stays disconnected from the main graph no matter how many identities it spawns. A periodic pulse of fresh verifiable work keeps stale vertices from coasting on old reputation, and any vertex whose pulse lapses decays toward zero. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a dense, long-lived, mutually attested subgraph that survives the pulse is expensive, so the attack cost scales with the graph it must fake.
